evidence: Receiving DO2 trajectory 14.8→9.6 mg/L over 0–52 h, minimum constraint 2.0 mg/L
Receiving P(48h)=2.87 g/L matches source range 2.98–3.06 g/L
Source batches show P rising to ~8 g/L at 72 h then declining, indicating normal phase progression with remaining productive window
args.rationale: Receiving fermentation is healthy and on the source-calibrated trajectory: DO2 ≈ 9.6 mg/L at the 52 h decision time (well above the 2.0 mg/L minimum), product at 2.87 g/L (48 h assay) matching the source batches' 2.98–3.06 g/L at the same age. Source batches peaked near 8 g/L around 72 h and declined thereafter, so the process is mid-production with no oxygen limitation and no feed/aeration anomaly. Any feed reduction would reduce product formation; increased aeration is unnecessary since oxygen is not limiting; a stop would forfeit production. No intervention needed.
args.uncertainty: Source and receiving processes differ in hidden parameters; a future DO2 sag similar to the transient dips seen in sources (e.g., ~8 mg/L around 55–75 h) could occur but remains far above the 2.0 mg/L constraint. Late-phase product decline after ~72 h is expected in sources; timing in receiving may shift. Assay availability is delayed 4 h, so current product state is partially stale.
